hero.title: What is a
hero.description: A state-recognised foundation year that turns a non-German school certificate into a full German university entrance qualification. Pass it, and you can study almost anywhere in Germany.

journey.title: Your path to a
journey.description: Five clear steps separate you from a German university place. Here is how the whole journey fits together.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.title: Application
steps.description: Apply through uni-assist or directly to the Studienkolleg. First check your certificate in the anabin / DAAD database.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.title: Entrance exam
steps.description: Sit the Aufnahmeprüfung — a German test plus a subject test matched to your chosen track.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.title: Two semesters
steps.description: Study your subjects entirely in German, with language teaching that lifts you from B2 towards C1.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.title: Feststellungsprüfung
steps.description: Take the final FSP assessment — the exam that certifies you are ready for German university study.

steps.label: Step 5
steps.title: University
steps.description: With a passed FSP your qualification is recognised nationwide. Apply for your degree across Germany.

why.title: Why it exists
why.description: Not every foreign school-leaving certificate counts as a German university entrance qualification. The Studienkolleg closes that gap.

bridge.title: Bridge your education
bridge.description: It fills the gap between your home school system and German academic standards, so you start your degree on equal footing.

german.title: Master academic German
german.description: Subjects are taught in German, building the lecture, exam and academic-writing skills a degree demands — up to C1.

path.title: A recognised path
path.description: Pass the FSP and your qualification is valid at universities throughout Germany, not just the one that hosted you.

courses.title: Choose your track
courses.description: University Studienkollegs run five specialised tracks (Schwerpunktkurse). You pick one based on the degree you intend to study.

T.description: The largest track — for engineering, mathematics and the natural sciences.
T.examples: Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Computer Science

M.description: For medical, biological and pharmaceutical degree programmes.

W.description: For business, economics and most social-science degrees.

G.description: For the humanities, arts, German studies and related fields.
G.examples: History, Philosophy, Law, Journalism, Art History

S.description: For language and linguistics degrees in languages other than German.

courses.fhNote: Heading for a University of Applied Sciences (Fachhochschule)? Those run their own, more practice-oriented tracks — TI (technical), WW (economics), GD (design & arts) and SW (social work).

eligibility.title: Check before you apply
eligibility.description: Whether you need a Studienkolleg depends entirely on how Germany rates your school certificate. Look yourself up in the anabin / DAAD database first.

direct.title: You can skip it
direct.description: Your certificate already counts as a full entrance qualification (HZB). You may apply straight to a German university.

restricted.title: Partly recognised
restricted.description: You can study only certain fields directly. For anything outside them, a Studienkolleg and the FSP are required.

kolleg.title: This is your route
kolleg.description: Your certificate isn't recognised for direct entry. A Studienkolleg plus the FSP is the standard path to any German degree.

requirements.title: What you need to apply
requirements.description: Exact documents and deadlines vary by Studienkolleg, but almost every application asks for the same essentials.

language.title: German language
items: Minimum B1 to apply — B2 is strongly recommended
Most public Studienkollegs require B2 for the entrance exam
Goethe, telc, TestDaF or DSH certificates are accepted

documents.title: Documents
items: Passport, biometric photo & proof of health insurance
Short CV and letter of motivation

finances.title: Costs & finances
items: Blocked account for your visa: ≈ €11,904 / year (2026)

timeline.title: Application windows
timeline.note: Each Studienkolleg sets its own deadline — always confirm on its website.

fsp.title: The Feststellungsprüfung (FSP)
fsp.description: The Studienkolleg ends with the FSP — the assessment that certifies you are ready for German university study and unlocks admission nationwide.

tested.title: What's tested
tested.description: German plus the core subjects of your track — exactly the knowledge your future degree builds on.

format.title: Format
format.description: Written exams across several days, with oral examinations in some subjects.

after.title: After passing
after.description: Your qualification is recognised across Germany. Apply for degrees in your field at any university.

cta.title: Ready to start your journey?
cta.description: Explore Studienkollegs across Germany and prepare for the entrance exam with a structured, daily plan.
